newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Oct 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Oct 10.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- KWV has unveiled plans to transform the grape and wine-producing co-operative into a public company, a move which would result in unbundling of all its assets for distribution to member farmers.
- Posts and Telecommunications Minister Jay Naidoo on Wednesday berated advertisers for withdrawing support from the SABC because "too many black faces were being shown on television".

- The National Party on Wednesday denied that it received a donation from Sol Kerzner during F.W. de Klerk's term as president, but the hotel magnate said last night that he had donated 50,000 rand "sometime in 1994".

- The Print, Paper, Wood and Allied Workers Union (Ppwawu) on Wednesday threatened Sappi Ltd with a strike if it failed to take disciplinary action against Roland Mazery, the managing director of Sappi Saiccor. Mazery is behind a campaign to draw international attention to South Africa's crime problem.
- Societe Generale, France's second largest bank, said on Wednesday it had bought a 51 percent stake in local stockbroking firm Frankel Pollak for an undisclosed sum.
- Scottish and Newcastle, the largest British brewing company, has snapped up a 75 percent stake in Mitchell's Brewery, a niche player in the South African beer market, in a multimillion rand deal.

- Investec, South Africa's fifth largest banking group, is in advanced negotiations" to acquire the British stokebrokerage Carr Shepards, which has more than 2.5 billion pounds in funds under management or advice.
- Hundreds of hijack victims queued for hours in the Johannesburg sun on Wednesday in the hope of identifying their attackers in a mass idnetity parade.
- Two more SAA international flights -- to Perth/Sydney and Munich/Dusseldorf -- were cancelled last night as the airline continued to lock out employees.
